newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count up 10 to 915 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count up 10 to 915 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 915 as of March 27, up 10 from the prior week and 187 above the year-ago total of 728, Baker Hughes Inc. reported Thursday.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by three to 760, while rigs working offshore rose by two to 126.

The number of rigs active in inland waters rose by three to 29. Among individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Louisiana, which was up by 10, Texas, which was up by two, and Wyoming, which was up by two.
The Gulf of Mexico rose by four to 121.

A total of 400 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up 21 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas was down by 11 to 514, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at one.
In Canada, the number of working rigs was down 54 at 323 vs. 196 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
